what_this_is: The presentation film, described by the sources that build it. Every field below is derived from presentation/src at generation time rather than read from a document, so nothing written by hand can disagree with it about the same film.

beats.name: Hello
beats.narration: Hello everyone. This one is real. On a Sunday night in August, a volunteer pointed a radio at the sky and caught 4 minutes of a satellite. The record for it says two words. with-signal.

beats.name: Title
beats.narration: Nobody went back to it. It is one of two thousand seven hundred and twenty seven.

beats.name: Problem
beats.narration: Only seven hundred and thirty nine carry a human verdict. The rest were kept and never read, because there is no order to work through them in.

beats.name: Physics
beats.narration: A pass shifts the frequency you hear. The orbit predicts that curve, spanning seventeen thousand two hundred and ninety hertz. Slide it one hundred and thirteen pixels and it lands on the trace. The gap, as a fraction of the frequency, is plus thirty two point zero five parts per million. This station had already corrected for Doppler, and nothing in the record says so.

beats.name: Queue
beats.narration: That is what the queue ranks on. four hundred and seven observations against a budget of 50. Not the loudest. The ones where the evidence disagrees with itself.

beats.name: Live
beats.narration: All of that was frozen in August. Here is the live console measuring one again. Of 10 quantities, 8 match the archived digits exactly.

beats.name: Flow
beats.narration: You can drive the same evidence from a LangFlow canvas. Watch. A sentence goes in with a frequency this observation does not have. One take, no cut. The checker refuses it and names why.

beats.name: Session
beats.narration: ungrounded number. That is the same checker that decides whether our own generated notes ship.

beats.name: Result
beats.narration: Now the part demos skip. Six gates, with thresholds, written before anything was measured. The headline one wanted half again as many conflicts as random. This queue found 20 of them. Random ordering, at the same budget, expects 12.6. We publish that as not established.

beats.name: Gates
beats.narration: The point estimate is 1.58, and the interval straddles the bar, so it fails here. 3 of 6 gates met, and nothing was moved.

beats.name: Established
beats.narration: Three did come back decided. Evidence tools take a local Granite model from 2 of 24 right to 22. The checker caught every one of five hundred and twenty five planted falsehoods. And on stations the queue never saw, lift clears at 2.25.

beats.name: Bob
beats.narration: IBM Bob built the load-bearing pipeline: contracts, snapshot, parser, corridor, baselines, queue. 10 dated units, each naming what it changed and what failed first.

beats.name: Colophon
beats.narration: Every figure you heard came out of a receipt. The waterfall is public, cited and licensed.

beats.name: Thanks
beats.narration: That is TraceTriage. Thank you for watching. Go and check a number.

claims.reading: A claim is a value resolved from a key path in one of the files below at build time. The ones read and never drawn are cross-checks the test suite uses, not figures on screen.

what_this_does_not_measure: Whether the film is any good, or whether a viewer follows it.
Whether the rendered file plays. The digests say only that the committed bytes are the bytes this receipt was written about.

Whether the numbers are right. They are the receipts' own numbers, and each receipt's own study is what establishes them. This receipt establishes only that the film reads them rather than restating them.
